subject.title: feat: raise (or remove) 3-minute no-output watchdog cap on CLI requests

question: Should ordinary inherited resumed CLI-backed user runs keep the 180-second guard, move to a longer bounded default, or gain explicit disable/tuning semantics?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves the inherited resume guard after the configured-timeout fix, and changing the default or disable semantics trades off long-task availability against stuck-process recovery for existing users.

options.title: Approve a bounded longer default
options.body: Raise the inherited resume ceiling through the existing watchdog defaults, keep the watchdog enabled, and require resolver plus real behavior proof for long silent work and stalled-process recovery.

options.title: Add explicit disable/tuning semantics
options.body: Accept 0/null-style disable behavior only with schema, docs, upgrade, and compatibility proof for existing configs.

options.title: Keep the 180-second inherited guard
options.body: Leave current behavior intact and document per-backend watchdog overrides for operators with known long silent CLI workloads.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded longer default
recommendation.body: Raise the inherited resume ceiling through the existing watchdog defaults, keep the watchdog enabled, and require resolver plus real behavior proof for long silent work and stalled-process recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent PR 90912 review and co-authorship is the strongest available signal for the remaining timeout-policy choice.
